chapter: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
title: McKinney's Synco Septet and Claude Jones's advice to take up trombone
summary: He listened to McKinney's septet rehearse; Claude Jones, who married his sister, urged him to take up trombone because good Black trombonists were scarce.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: What was the first, your first interest in getting to hear an orchestra where you figured you wanted to play in an orchestra? How did you get to there?
Well, McKinney had a band called Synco Cinco Septet. They only had seven pieces. And they used to rehearse out to Milt Senior's house, you know.
And I used to go out there and listen. And Claude Jones was playing with the band at the time and he finally married my sister.
And Claude usually -- he played such great trombone. To me I thought he was the greatest trombone player that ever lived.

So he used to come home all the time, you know, come through Springfield, and he said, "Gee whiz, Quent," he said, "you've got such a good musical background, why don't you take the trombone? Because there's very few good colored trombone players. This would be a good instrument for you." So I thought over this thing and thought over this thing and finally the guys at home, my buddies, they got a band together and they had nine pieces. They needed a trombone to make ten pieces.
